citations.assessment: Both parses are in the same Rashi gloss, and the first-person second parse is explicitly Rashi’s.
The stated legal ruling is transmitted by the named Oshaya Zeira of Chavraya.
Rashi attributes the identifying epithet to the presence of another Oshaya. The citizens attest his motives in the adjacent narrative.
Tosafot explicitly explains Chavraya as a place name and cites the Avimi passage.
The midrash records Avimi min Chavraya in the context of the effect of rains on the ill. Tosafot’s quotation and the current midrash retain slightly different formulations.
The target attributes the place-name explanation to Mattenot Kehunah invoking Tosafot.
This baraita uses the full epithet. Rashi has no direct comment at the named unit. Tosafot comments about the spine and menstrual-tractate baraita but does not discuss the epithet.
